beats.text: The first hairline crack came from a war hero, in 1952 and again in 1956.
Texas voted for the Republican Dwight *Eisenhower* for president.
Lots of conservative Democrats were happy to vote Republican at the top of
the ticket and Democrat everywhere else.
Then in 1961, Lyndon Johnson left his Senate seat to become vice president.
There was a special election to replace him.
The Democrats were *split*.
Their candidate was a conservative oilman, and many liberal Democrats
simply refused to vote for him.
Some of them stayed home.
Some voted Republican just to send a message.
A young Republican professor named John Tower won by less than two points.
He became the first Republican elected statewide in Texas since Reconstruction.
On November 22nd, 1963, President John F. Kennedy was shot and killed in Dallas.
Lyndon Johnson, a Texan, was sworn in as president on Air Force One.
The next year, Johnson pushed through the Civil Rights Act of
1964, outlawing segregation, then the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
There is a famous line that Johnson said the Democrats had just
"lost the South for a generation."
Historians argue about whether he really said it, and exactly
how, but the direction was clear.
The national Democratic Party was now the party of civil rights, and
many conservative white Southerners began to look for the *door*.
